la:verb:revoco.gloss: to recall (troops, etc.), to call back
senses: to recall (troops, etc.), to call back
to regain, recover, bring back, restore
la:verb:revoco.html:
rĕ-vŏco, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
To call back, recall (class. and freq., esp. in the trop. sense).
Lit.
In gen.: quotiens foras ire volo, me retines, revocas,; cf. : de meo cursu rei publicae sum voce revocatus,: aliquem ex itinere,; ; : revocatus de exsilio Camillus,: revocatum ex provinciā,: Caesar in Italiam revocabatur,: spes Campanae defectionis Samnites rursus ad Caudium revocavit,: quid me intro revocas?.— Absol.: heus abiit: quin revocas?; ; : exclusit; revocat; redeam?; ; ; : abeo; et revocas nono post mense,; .—
Transf., of things, to draw or fetch back, to withdraw, turn back, etc.: lumina revocata,: oculos meos,: cupidas manus,: pedem ab alto,; cf. gradum,: deficientem capillum a vertice,to stroke back,: habenas,: manus post terga,to bind,: proscissam terram in liram,to bring back, restore,; cf.: in vitibus revocantur ea, quae, etc.,are pruned,; v.infra, B. 1. — Poet.: gelidos artus in vivum calorem,.—
In partic.
Milit. t. t.
To call back, recall; to call off, withdraw soldiers from a march or from any enterprise: his rebus cognitis Caesar legiones equitatumque revocari atque itinere desistere jubet,: insequentes nostros, ne longius prosequerentur, Sulla revocavit,; : quae receptui canunt, ut eos etiam revocent,: tardius revocati proelio excesserant,; cf. : equites,: reliquas copias,: naves omnes,: hos certo signo,fin.; 1, 28: milites ab opere,: legiones ab opere,: aestus crescens revocaverat fatigatos,.—
To recall to duty soldiers from a furlough: milites,: veteranos,: inter ceteros conveteranos suos revocatus,.—
In gen., to call back, recall: (Neptunus Tritona) jubet fluctus et flumina signo Jam revocare dato,.—
A theatrical t. t., to call for the repetition of a speech, a vocal performance, etc., to call back a player; to encore: Livius (Andronicus), cum saepius revocatus vocem obtudisset, etc.,: Diphilus tragoedus revocatus aliquoties a populo,: quoties ego hunc (sc. Archiam) vidi magnum numerum versuum dicere ex tempore! quoties revocatum eandem rem dicere commutatis verbis atque sententiis,: revocatus praeco, iterum pronunciavit eadem,.—Also with an inanim. object: cum Orestem fabulam doceret Euripides, primos tres versus revocasse dicitur Socrates,to have encored,. —Absol.: revocasse et repeti coëgisse,.—Impers. pass.: nominatim sum appellatus in Bruto Tullius qui libertatem civibus stabiliverat. Milies revocatum est,.—
To recall from death, bring back to life: quā servetis revocatum a morte Dareta,; cf.: Paeoniis revocatum herbis et amore Dianae,: dysentericos a morte revocari,.—
Trop.
In gen., to call back, recall, resume; to withdraw, retire; to regain, recover; to draw back, draw off or away; to withhold, restrain, etc.: facilius sicut in vitibus revocantur ea, quae sese nimium profuderunt,are checked, pruned,: et vires et corpus amisi: sed si morbum depulero, facile illa revocabo, will regain, recover, : quae (studia) remissa temporibus, longo intervallo intermissa revocavi,; cf.: quod, utcunque praetermissum, revocari non posset,: praetermissa,: quae (philosophia) nunc prope dimissa revocatur,: veteres artes,: priscos mores,: antiquam duramque militiam,: quaedam exoleta,: omissa,; et saep.: nonnumquam animum incitatum revoco ipse et reflecto,; cf. : vinolenti dubitant, haesitant, revocant se interdum,recover themselves, bethink themselves,: ut quaedam contra naturam depravata restituerentur et corrigerentur ab naturā, cum se ipsa revocasset aut arte atque medicinā,had recovered herself,: revocare se non poterat familiaritate implicatus,could not withdraw,: primae revocabo exordia pugnae,; cf. : revocari in memoriam somnii,; .— Poet., with inf.: nec tamen illa suae revocatur parcere famae, nor can she be induced, persuaded, etc., : memoriam ad referendam gratiam admonitione revocare,to bring, induce,: scalam nobis in memoriam revocare, , 16, 38, 2; : in memoriam rursus revocatus,: revocat tua forma parentem (with recordor),: magni est ingenii revocare mentem a sensibus,; cf.: eos ab illā consuetudine,: quos (homines) spes praedandi studiumque bellandi ab agriculturā et cottidiano labore revocabat,: aliquam a cupiditate,: aliquem a turpissimo consilio,: aliquem a tanto scelere,; cf. : animum ab irā,: jam lapsos ab errore,: perterritos animos a metu, et saep.: ab errore ad rectiorem viam,: cum ex saevis et perditis rebus ad meliorem statum fortuna revocatur, Cic. ap. : disceptationem ab rege ad Romanos revocabant,: rebus institutis ad humanitatem atque mansuetudinem revocavit animos hominum studiis bellandi jam immanes ac feros,: ad quam eos quasi formulam dicendi revocent,: ad quae me exempla revocas,; : rem paene ad manus,: me ad pristina studia revocavi,: me ad meum munus pensumque revocabo,: se ad industriam,: se rursus ad moestitiam,: se ad se,: vilicum ad rationem,compel to an account,: libertinos ingratos revocavit in servitutem,: fortunae possessionesque omnium in dubium incertumque revocabuntur,: ad spem consulatūs in partem revocandam aspirare non auderet,to bring over to his side,: quod temporis hortorum aut villarum curae seponitur, in animum revocabo,will transfer to my mind,: abi, Quo blandae juvenum te revocant preces (= a me ad se vocant, Orell.),.—
In partic.
Pregn.: ad aliquid, to apply, reduce, refer a thing to something as a standard (syn. referre) (Ciceron.): impuri cujusdam et ambitiosi et omnia ad suam potentiam revocantis esse sententiam,: misericordiā movetur, si is, qui audit, adduci potest, ut illa, quae de altero deplorentur, ad suas res revocet,: omnia ad artem et ad praecepta,: omnia ad scientiam,: illa de urbis situ ad rationem,: rationem ad veritatem,: rem ad illam rationem conjecturamque,.—
To recall, revoke, retract, cancel (not so till after the Aug. per.): si facta mihi revocare liceret. : promissum suum,: sententiam suam,: libertatem (shortly after: in servitutem retrahi),: litteras,: legatum ad quingenta,.—
As law t. t.: domum, domum suam revocare, to appeal to a judge of one's own country or city: (legatis) revocandi domum suam jus datur, , §§ 3, 4, and 5.—
To ask back again, to invite in return: mutuo vocare, Non. (rare): domum suam istum non fere quisquam vocabat. Nec mirum; qui neque in urbe viveret neque revocaturus esset,; Varr. ap. : cum vulpem revocasset,; .—Hence, transf.: tribuni plebis quoniam adhuc praesens certamen contentionemque fugerunt: nunc in meam contionem prodeant, et, quo provocati ad me venire noluerunt, revocati saltem revertantur,i. e. now that they are invited to come back,.—
To call again, summon anew (rare): itaque hominem populus revocat, et retrahatur necesse est,i. e. to answer a renewed accusation, (6), 6: tribuni de integro agere coeperunt revocaturosque se easdem tribus renuntiarunt,; cf. : refectum est convivium et rursus Quartilla ad bibendum revocavit,challenged us again,: convivam in diem posterum,.

la:verb:revertor.html:
rĕ-verto (-vort-) and rĕ-vertor (-vort-), versus (-vors-) (
inf. paragog. revertier, ), 3 (the authors of the ante-Aug. per. make the perfect forms, with the exception of the part. reversus, only from the active root, reverti, reverteram, revertisse, etc., :

; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.: reversus,; ; Dietsch; but cf.: reversus sum, etc.,; ; ; ; ; ; ; . But in the present tenses the active form is rare: revortit,; , and Pompon. ap. ; or Com. Rel. p. 201 Rib.: revertebant,; cf. Neue, Formenl. 2, p. 345 sq.; Zumpt, Gram. § 209 fin.) [verto], to turn back, turn about; to come back, return (syn.: redeo, revenio).

Lit.: clamitant me ut revertar,: (Deiotarus) cum ex itinere revertisset ... persaepe revertit ex itinere,; cf. : eodem (vultu) semper se vidisse exeuntem illum domo et revertentem,: ita maestus rediit, ut retractus, non reversus videretur,: reversus ille, etc.,: (mulier) per propinquos rogata, ut rediret, non est reversa, et saep.: cum ego a foro revortor,: a Fabricio ponte,: a Scythiā,; : reverti ab exsilio,; ; : a bello,; ; for which poet.: silvā,: jam ad te revortar,: ad aliquem,; ; et saep.: nisi domum revorteris,; so, domum, (opp. egredior); 70; 2, 3, 99; (opp. egressi); : Formias,: Ameriam,: Epheso Laodiceam,: hunc in locum,: in castra,: ad assuetas sibi sedes,: huc,; ; ; (opp. hinc profecti). — With double nom.: consules praedā ingenti partā victores reverterunt,. —
Of things: sol inde (sc. a brumalibus flexibus) revortens,: revertitur idem sol sub terras,: revertitur luna ad signum quodque,: multa videbis retro repulsa revorti,: retroque a terrā cunctā revorti,: quis neget . . . Tiberim reverti,: sol reversus,. —
Trop.
In gen., to return: nescit vox missa reverti,; cf. : leti jam limine ab ipso Ad vitam possint revorti,: ad superiorem consuetudinem,: ad illum animum meum pristinum,: ad sanitatem,: ad corporis commodum,: haec ad easdem particulas,: ad Musas,: ad bonam vitae consuetudinem,: ut reverteretur in gratiam mecum,: poena in caput tuum,; cf. . —
In partic., in speech (after a digression), to return, revert to a theme, etc.: scribam tibi tres libros, ad quos revertare,: discedo parumper a somniis, ad quae mox revertar,: sed, ut ad propositum revertamur, etc.,: ut ad me revertar,: ad illam puellam exposititiam,: proinde ad id revertar,: illuc,. — In a comic equivoque: revortor rursus denuo Carthaginem, Si quid mandare voltis aut curarier,.

la:verb:reviso.html:
rĕ-vīso, ĕre, v. n. and a.
Neutr., to look back on a thing, come back or again to see (cf. respicio); to pay a visit again (ante- and post-class.): ut ad me revisas,: ad me,: ad stabulum,.— Poet.: signa ad lunam,: reviso quid agant, aut quid captent consili,; : inde redit rabies eadem et furor ille revisit,i. e. comes back, returns,.—
Act., to go or come to see again; to revisit: tu modo nos revise aliquando,: cum poteris, revises nos,: sed tu velim ... nos aliquando revisas,; : ipsa sedesque Revisit Laeta suas,: vates tuus te reviset,: urbem (with petere),: rem Gallicanam,: negotia sua cottidie,, praef. § 8: agrum saepius,.—With things as subjects: longos obitus (sidera),: aut quae digna satis fortuna revisit?: multos aeterna revisens Fortuna,.

la:verb:revolvo.gloss: to roll back; unroll, unwind; revolve, return
senses: to roll back; unroll, unwind; revolve, return
to turn over, read over, repeat
to relate again, repeat; reenact; brood or reflect upon
to come or go back, return, recur, relapse
la:verb:revolvo.html:
rĕ-volvo, volvi, vŏlūtum, 3, v. a.,
to roll back; to unroll, unwind; to revolve, return (class.; esp. freq. since the Aug. per.).
Lit.
In gen.: Draco revolvens Sese, Cic. poët. N. D. 2, 42, 106: (pelagus) gelidum ab imo fluctum revolvit in partem superiorem,: fluctus (hibernus auster),: retro Aestum (ventus),: retro sua fila (Sorores),; cf.: inmites scis nulla revolvere Parcas Stamina,: lapidem,. — Poet.: (pontus) aestu revoluta resorbens Saxa,i. e. from which the waves are rolled back,: addiderat Civilis obliquam in Rhenum molem, cujus objectu revolutus amnis adjacentibus superfunderetur,: rursus perplexum iter omne revolvens Fallacis silvae,going over again,: revoluta aequora, Wagn. —
Mid., to come or go back, to revolve, return, etc. (syn. revertor): itaque revolvor identidem in Tusculanum,: ter sese attollens cubitoque annixa levavit: Ter revoluta toro est,fell back, sank back,: spissā jacuit revolutus harenā,: revoluta rursus eodem est, (a little before: relapsa est).— Poet., of returning time: dies,: saecula,; cf.: centesimā revolvente se lunā,: saecula revolvuntur,.—
In partic., to unroll, turn over, read over, repeat (not ante-Aug.; syn. verso): tuas adversus te Origines revolvam,: taedium illud et scripta et lecta saepius revolvendi,: cum loca jam recitata revolvimus irrevocati,: antiqua,; ; .—
Trop.
In gen.: in iis, quae denominata sunt, summa paupertas in eadem nos frequentissime revolvit,leads back,: iterum revolvere casus Iliacos, to go through again, to undergo or experience again, .—
Mid., to return to any thing; with in: in eandem vitam te revolutum denuo Video esse,; cf.: in luxuriam,: in metus,: in ista,: animus in sollicitudinem revolutus est,: iterum in pejora revolvi,

: rursus in veterem fato revoluta figuram,.— With ad: omnia necessario a tempore atque homine ad communes rerum et generum summas revolventur,: ad patris revolvor sententiam,: ad ejus causae seposita argumenta revolvi nos oportet,: ad illa elementa,: ad dispensationem annonae,: ad vana et totiens irrisa,: ad memoriam conjugii et infantiam liberorum,: ad vitia,: ad irritum (labor et victoria),: rursus ad superstitionem,.— With adv.: primum eodem revolveris,: eo, quo minime volt, revolvitur,: cum majore periculo eodem revolvuntur,; cf.: eo revolvi rem, ut, etc.,.—

In partic., to relate again, repeat; to brood or reflect upon (not anteAug.): sed quid ego haec nequicquam ingrata revolvo?: facta,: dicta factaque ejus secum,: iras in animo,; : visa, (with secum jussa refert): curas (animus), (with repetit metus).

la:noun:reversio.gloss: The act of turning back (before reaching a destination), return.
senses: The act of turning back (before reaching a destination), return.
The act of returning or coming around again.
la:noun:reversio.html:
rĕversĭo (rĕvors-), ōnis, f.
reverto
.
A turning back before reaching one's destination (differing from reditus, a coming back, return): quam valde ille reditu vel potius reversione meă laetatus,: exponam vobis breviter consilium et profectionis et reversionis meae,: reversionem ut ad me faceret denuo,; ; Varr. ap. ; . —
Of things in gen., a returning, return: febrium,: annua (solis),; cf. in plur.: planetarum temporum,.—
Trop., gram. t. t. for ἀναστροφή,an inversion of words (like mecum, secum, quibus de rebus), .

la:verb:revincio.gloss: to bind back, tie back, fasten around
senses: to bind back, tie back, fasten around
la:verb:revincio.html:
rĕ-vincĭo, vinxi, vinctum, 4, v. a.
To bind back or backwards; to bind around, bind fast, fasten (class.; not in Cic.).
Lit.: nisi esset (terra) caelo revincta,: ancorae pro funibus ferreis catenis revinctae,: tignis in contrariam partem revinctis,; cf.: trabes introrsus,: stipites demissi et ab infimo revincti,: navigium (with religare),: aliquem ad saxa,to bind fast,; cf.: zonam de poste,: errantem Mycono e celsā Gyaroque revinxit,: caput tortā angue, bound around, Varr. Atacin. ap. P.; cf.: latus ense,to gird, (4, 13), 11: templum Velleribus niveis et festā fronde revinctum,.— In a Greek construction: ecce manūs juvenem interea post terga revinctum trahebant,with his hands tied behind him,: qui recitat lanā fauces et colla revinctus,wrapped up,.— Poet.: latices in glaciem revincti,bound, stiffened,.—
Trop., to bind, fasten, etc.: mentem amore,: urbes legibus,: te sibi generum fraternā prole, id. Nupt. Honor. et Mar. 36: miserā in peste revinctos confodiunt,; .—*
To unbind, loose: quempiam (opp. alligare, and = resolvere),.

la:verb:revello.html:
rĕ-vello, velli, vulsum or volsum, 3, v. a.,
to pluck or pull away, to pull or tear out, to tear off or away (freq. and class.).
Lit.: tela de corpore,: nascentis equi de fronte revolsus amor,: titulum de fronte,: telum altā ab radice,: caput a cervice,; cf.: cornu a fronte,: saxum e monte,: partem e monte,: a silvis silvas et ab arvis arva,: ab aliquo morte revelli,to be torn away,: scuta manibus,: axem temone,; cf.: sudem osse,: arborem manibus tellure,: quos Sidoniā urbe,to tear away, remove,: puerum,: solio regem,: herbas radice,with the root,; so, too, annosam pinum solido trunco,: illam crucem, quae fixa est ad portum,: tabulam,, § 112: Gorgonis os pulcherrimum revellit atque abstulit,, § 124: gradus,: saepta,: claustra,; : janua, quā effractā et revolsā, tota pateret provincia,: vincula,: paene fores templi,: templa,: revulsis venis,opened,: scuta manibus,: pellem,: stipites revincti, ne revelli possent,: proximos agri terminos,to tear away, remove,: signa (when an army decamps),; : curvo dente humum,to tear up,; cf.: majorum sepulcra,. — Poet.: cinerem manesque,to disturb, violate,.—
Trop., to tear away, send away, etc.: cujus totus consulatus est ex omni monumentorum memoriā revulsus,: injurias honorificis verbis,: alicui avias veteres,prejudices,: falsorum persuasionem,: penitus de stirpe imperium,: oscula fida, (with dissipat amplexus).
la:verb:revello.inflection: velli, vulsum or volsum, 3, v. a.

la:verb:revomo.html:
rĕ-vŏmo, ŭi, 3, v. a.,
to spew or vomit forth again; to vomit up, disgorge (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.: salsos pectore fluctus,: plumam avibus devoratis (dracones),: haustum mare (Charybdis),; cf. ; and of the same: vorat haec raptas revomitque carinas,; cf.: umorque aquae sursum revomit atque remittit (tigna),: spolia assidue mota ventis maria revomebant,cast up again,: at miseri fluctant revomentes aequora nautae,.—*
Trop.: cum sanguine et spiritu male partam revomuere victoriam,.

la:verb:reveho.gloss: to carry, bear or convey back
senses: to carry, bear or convey back
la:verb:reveho.html:
rĕ-vĕho, xi, ctum, 3, v. a.,
to carry or bring back, to convey back (class.; syn.:

reporto, refero, reddo).

Lit.: Diana Segestam Carthagine revecta,; so, praedam inde,: tela ad Graios,: aliquem domum (mater),; ; : Promethea (satelles Orci),: arma,: exsequias Romam,: revehunt vitrea, et aëna, vestis, fibulas,.—
Pass., in mid. force, to drive, ride, sail, etc., back; to return: ne quis reveheretur inde ad proelium,: equo citato ad urbem revectus,; : consul revectus in castra,: per circum ad foros,: curru triumphali revectus est,: non satis est Ithacam revehi?: hac ego sum raptis parte revectus equis,.—
Trop.: famam optimam ex Bithyniā revexisti,brought back, brought home,: ad paulo superiorem aetatem revecti sumus,have gone back,.

la:verb:revelo.html:
rĕ-vēlo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to unveil, uncover, lay bare (not ante-Aug.; syn.: patefacio, aperio, nudo, retego).
Lit.: caput (opp. involvere),: frontem,: os,: pectus,: carpenta (opp. contegere),: sacra,. —
Trop., to disclose, reveal: fraudes (with detegere),: omnia (tempus),: justitiam et salutem Domini cunctis gentibus,; ; et saep.: Ulixes Eumaeo, quis sit, revelat. .

la:adv:revera.gloss: in reality; in fact; in practice
senses: in reality; in fact; in practice

la:noun:revelatio.html:
rĕvēlātĭo, ōnis, f.
revelo
,
an uncovering, laying bare (eccl. Lat.).
Lit.: pudendorum,. —
Trop.: imaginariae revelationes,: filii sui,a revelation,; . — Esp.,the Revelation of St. John,.

la:noun:reverentia.html:
rĕvĕrentĭa, ae, f.
revereor
,
timidity arising from high respect or (more rarely) from fear, respect, regard, fear, awe, reverence (not freq. till after the post-Aug. per.): adhibenda est quaedam reverentia adversus homines, et optimi cujusque et reliquorum: nam neglegere, quid de se quisque sentiat, non solum arrogantis est, sed omnino dissoluti,: personae,: judicum,: senatus,: nulla superiorum,: sacramenti,: imperii,; : legum,: famae,: quorum reverentia movit Saepe deos,: veri,: recti et aequi,: nulla poscendi, dandi,shyness, shame, (4, 12), 13: discendi,fear,: ut cuique personae debetur reverentia,; cf. : maxima debetur puero reverentia,; judex tacitus reverentiam postulat,: mihi reverentiā ut aequali habebatur,: quam illa reverentiam marito suo praestitit,: mihi reverentiam praestat, (11), 1.— Pass., deference, regard, etc.: ego reverentiae vestrae sic semper inserviam (for vestri), the deference or veneration due to you, your dignity, —Reverentia, as a deity, the mother of Majestas by Honor, .

inf. paragog. revertier, ), 3 (the authors of the ante-Aug. per. make the perfect forms, with the exception of the part. reversus, only from the active root, reverti, reverteram, revertisse, etc., :

; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.: reversus,; ; Dietsch; but cf.: reversus sum, etc.,; ; ; ; ; ; ; . But in the present tenses the active form is rare: revortit,; , and Pompon. ap. ; or Com. Rel. p. 201 Rib.: revertebant,; cf. Neue, Formenl. 2, p. 345 sq.; Zumpt, Gram. § 209 fin.) [verto], to turn back, turn about; to come back, return (syn.: redeo, revenio).

Lit.: clamitant me ut revertar,: (Deiotarus) cum ex itinere revertisset ... persaepe revertit ex itinere,; cf. : eodem (vultu) semper se vidisse exeuntem illum domo et revertentem,: ita maestus rediit, ut retractus, non reversus videretur,: reversus ille, etc.,: (mulier) per propinquos rogata, ut rediret, non est reversa, et saep.: cum ego a foro revortor,: a Fabricio ponte,: a Scythiā,; : reverti ab exsilio,; ; : a bello,; ; for which poet.: silvā,: jam ad te revortar,: ad aliquem,; ; et saep.: nisi domum revorteris,; so, domum, (opp. egredior); 70; 2, 3, 99; (opp. egressi); : Formias,: Ameriam,: Epheso Laodiceam,: hunc in locum,: in castra,: ad assuetas sibi sedes,: huc,; ; ; (opp. hinc profecti). — With double nom.: consules praedā ingenti partā victores reverterunt,. —
Of things: sol inde (sc. a brumalibus flexibus) revortens,: revertitur idem sol sub terras,: revertitur luna ad signum quodque,: multa videbis retro repulsa revorti,: retroque a terrā cunctā revorti,: quis neget . . . Tiberim reverti,: sol reversus,. —
Trop.
In gen., to return: nescit vox missa reverti,; cf. : leti jam limine ab ipso Ad vitam possint revorti,: ad superiorem consuetudinem,: ad illum animum meum pristinum,: ad sanitatem,: ad corporis commodum,: haec ad easdem particulas,: ad Musas,: ad bonam vitae consuetudinem,: ut reverteretur in gratiam mecum,: poena in caput tuum,; cf. . —
In partic., in speech (after a digression), to return, revert to a theme, etc.: scribam tibi tres libros, ad quos revertare,: discedo parumper a somniis, ad quae mox revertar,: sed, ut ad propositum revertamur, etc.,: ut ad me revertar,: ad illam puellam exposititiam,: proinde ad id revertar,: illuc,. — In a comic equivoque: revortor rursus denuo Carthaginem, Si quid mandare voltis aut curarier,.

la:verb:revelo#3.html:
rĕ-vēlo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to unveil, uncover, lay bare (not ante-Aug.; syn.: patefacio, aperio, nudo, retego).
Lit.: caput (opp. involvere),: frontem,: os,: pectus,: carpenta (opp. contegere),: sacra,. —
Trop., to disclose, reveal: fraudes (with detegere),: omnia (tempus),: justitiam et salutem Domini cunctis gentibus,; ; et saep.: Ulixes Eumaeo, quis sit, revelat. .

la:verb:revolvo#2.html:
rĕ-volvo, volvi, vŏlūtum, 3, v. a.,
to roll back; to unroll, unwind; to revolve, return (class.; esp. freq. since the Aug. per.).
Lit.
In gen.: Draco revolvens Sese, Cic. poët. N. D. 2, 42, 106: (pelagus) gelidum ab imo fluctum revolvit in partem superiorem,: fluctus (hibernus auster),: retro Aestum (ventus),: retro sua fila (Sorores),; cf.: inmites scis nulla revolvere Parcas Stamina,: lapidem,. — Poet.: (pontus) aestu revoluta resorbens Saxa,i. e. from which the waves are rolled back,: addiderat Civilis obliquam in Rhenum molem, cujus objectu revolutus amnis adjacentibus superfunderetur,: rursus perplexum iter omne revolvens Fallacis silvae,going over again,: revoluta aequora, Wagn. —
Mid., to come or go back, to revolve, return, etc. (syn. revertor): itaque revolvor identidem in Tusculanum,: ter sese attollens cubitoque annixa levavit: Ter revoluta toro est,fell back, sank back,: spissā jacuit revolutus harenā,: revoluta rursus eodem est, (a little before: relapsa est).— Poet., of returning time: dies,: saecula,; cf.: centesimā revolvente se lunā,: saecula revolvuntur,.—
In partic., to unroll, turn over, read over, repeat (not ante-Aug.; syn. verso): tuas adversus te Origines revolvam,: taedium illud et scripta et lecta saepius revolvendi,: cum loca jam recitata revolvimus irrevocati,: antiqua,; ; .—
Trop.
In gen.: in iis, quae denominata sunt, summa paupertas in eadem nos frequentissime revolvit,leads back,: iterum revolvere casus Iliacos, to go through again, to undergo or experience again, .—
Mid., to return to any thing; with in: in eandem vitam te revolutum denuo Video esse,; cf.: in luxuriam,: in metus,: in ista,: animus in sollicitudinem revolutus est,: iterum in pejora revolvi,

: rursus in veterem fato revoluta figuram,.— With ad: omnia necessario a tempore atque homine ad communes rerum et generum summas revolventur,: ad patris revolvor sententiam,: ad ejus causae seposita argumenta revolvi nos oportet,: ad illa elementa,: ad dispensationem annonae,: ad vana et totiens irrisa,: ad memoriam conjugii et infantiam liberorum,: ad vitia,: ad irritum (labor et victoria),: rursus ad superstitionem,.— With adv.: primum eodem revolveris,: eo, quo minime volt, revolvitur,: cum majore periculo eodem revolvuntur,; cf.: eo revolvi rem, ut, etc.,.—

In partic., to relate again, repeat; to brood or reflect upon (not anteAug.): sed quid ego haec nequicquam ingrata revolvo?: facta,: dicta factaque ejus secum,: iras in animo,; : visa, (with secum jussa refert): curas (animus), (with repetit metus).

la:adj:revolubilis.html:
rĕvŏlūbĭlis, e, adj.
revolvo
,
that may be rolled back (poet.): pondus (i. e. saxum),: unda,: orbita,.—Fig.: juro ego Fatorum nulli revolubile carmen,saxum,.

la:noun:revolutio.html:
rĕvŏlūtĭo, ōnis, f.
id.
,
a revolving, revolution (late Lat. for conversio), , 22, 12; ; .

la:verb:revereor.gloss: to stand in awe (of), regard, respect, honor, reverence, revere
senses: to stand in awe (of), regard, respect, honor, reverence, revere
to stand in fear (of); to be afraid, fear
la:verb:revereor.html:
rĕ-vĕrĕor, ĭtus. 2,
v. dep. a. (act. collat. form rĕvĕrĕo, acc. to P.), to stand in awe or fear of; to regard, respect, honor; to fear, be afraid of; to reverence, revere (ante-class. and post-Aug.; syn. veneror): Ap. Quid est quod pudendum siet, genere natam bono pauperem Ducere uxorem? Pe. Revereor filium, (cf. infra, the passage, ): observantia, per quam aetate aut sapientiā aut honore ... antecedentis reveremur et colimus, : hos (sc. oratores) ituri in provincias magistratus reverebantur, hos reversi colebant,: Nigidium Cicero summe reveritus est,.—More freq. with inanim. or abstr. objects: quasi ejus opulentitatem reverearis,stood in awe of,: simultatem meam, (also quoted in ): adventum tuom,: fulgorem ab auro,: dicam non reverens assentandi suspicionem,: multa adversa reverens,: virtutes,: coetum virorum (Tullia),: fortunam captivae,: auctoritatem illustrium scriptorum,: reverearis occursum, non reformides,: ne revereatur, minus jam quo redeat domum,: ne quaestus quidem suos reveritus illos opimos, etc.,i. e. did not spare,.—(*β) Impers. in analogy with pudet: non te tui saltem pudet, si nihil mei revereatur, Varr. ap. ; cf. vereor. — Hence,
rĕvĕrens, entis, P. a., respectful, regardful, reverent: sermo erga patrem imperatoremque reverens, de se moderatus,; cf.: responsum parum reverens, Massur. Sabin. ap. : ora,bashful, modest, (3, 28), 33: puella parentum suorum reverens,. — Comp.: nihilo reverentior leniorve erga senatum,: quis reverentior senatus candidatus?; cf. : sanctius ac reverentius visum de actis deorum credere quam scire,: illnd modestius ac fortasse reverentius,; cf.: nomen Augusti,.— Sup.: Gabium reverentissimum mei expertus, (18), 1. — Adv.: rĕvĕrenter, respectfully: aliquem adire,: amicos colere,. — Comp., .— Sup., ; ; (32) init. —
rĕvĕ-rendus, a, um, P. a., inspiring awe, venerable, reverend (mostly poet.; cf.: colen. dus, venerandus): nox,: facies,: sacraria,: vetustas (libri),; : vultu,: epulae,.— Sup.: Reverendissimus, most reverend, right reverend, a title of bishops, etc., Cod. Th 1, 55, 8; 1, 2, 6.

la:verb:reverso.html:
rĕverso, āre, v. freq. a.
id.
,
to turn round (late Lat.): versa et reversa in tergum et in latera,: panis qui non reversatur,: subcinericius panis est cinere coctus et reversatus,.— Mid.: reversatur ejus ex talis,.— Pass. reversatus, turned back: palpebra ejus,.

la:verb:revivisco.html:
rĕ-vīvisco (rĕvīvesco; v. Orell. ), vixi, 3,
v. inch. n., to come to life again, to be restored to life, to revive (class.; a favorite word with Cic., esp. in the trop. signif.).
Lit.: reviviscat M'. Curius aut eorum aliquis, etc.,; ; ; ; : ille reviviscet jam nunquam,: apes,: ut revixisse aut renatum sibi quisque Scipionem imperatorem dicat,: conchae,.—
Transf., to grow again: gramina, nisi manu eliguntur, revivescunt,: avulsae pennae (insectorum),.—
Trop., to revive, recover, gather strength, renew vigor, etc.: ipsa causa ea est, ut jam simul cum re publicā, necessario reviviscat atque recreetur,; cf. : omnes (civitatis) suis legibus et judiciis usae revixerunt,: res publica,: adventu nostro revivescunt justitia, abstinentia,: quo facilius reviviscat Pompeianorum causa toties jugulata, Anton. ap. : cum venisset mandatum, peccatum revixit,.

la:verb:revoco#2.html:
rĕ-vŏco, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
To call back, recall (class. and freq., esp. in the trop. sense).
Lit.
In gen.: quotiens foras ire volo, me retines, revocas,; cf. : de meo cursu rei publicae sum voce revocatus,: aliquem ex itinere,; ; : revocatus de exsilio Camillus,: revocatum ex provinciā,: Caesar in Italiam revocabatur,: spes Campanae defectionis Samnites rursus ad Caudium revocavit,: quid me intro revocas?.— Absol.: heus abiit: quin revocas?; ; : exclusit; revocat; redeam?; ; ; : abeo; et revocas nono post mense,; .—
Transf., of things, to draw or fetch back, to withdraw, turn back, etc.: lumina revocata,: oculos meos,: cupidas manus,: pedem ab alto,; cf. gradum,: deficientem capillum a vertice,to stroke back,: habenas,: manus post terga,to bind,: proscissam terram in liram,to bring back, restore,; cf.: in vitibus revocantur ea, quae, etc.,are pruned,; v.infra, B. 1. — Poet.: gelidos artus in vivum calorem,.—
In partic.
Milit. t. t.
To call back, recall; to call off, withdraw soldiers from a march or from any enterprise: his rebus cognitis Caesar legiones equitatumque revocari atque itinere desistere jubet,: insequentes nostros, ne longius prosequerentur, Sulla revocavit,; : quae receptui canunt, ut eos etiam revocent,: tardius revocati proelio excesserant,; cf. : equites,: reliquas copias,: naves omnes,: hos certo signo,fin.; 1, 28: milites ab opere,: legiones ab opere,: aestus crescens revocaverat fatigatos,.—
To recall to duty soldiers from a furlough: milites,: veteranos,: inter ceteros conveteranos suos revocatus,.—
In gen., to call back, recall: (Neptunus Tritona) jubet fluctus et flumina signo Jam revocare dato,.—
A theatrical t. t., to call for the repetition of a speech, a vocal performance, etc., to call back a player; to encore: Livius (Andronicus), cum saepius revocatus vocem obtudisset, etc.,: Diphilus tragoedus revocatus aliquoties a populo,: quoties ego hunc (sc. Archiam) vidi magnum numerum versuum dicere ex tempore! quoties revocatum eandem rem dicere commutatis verbis atque sententiis,: revocatus praeco, iterum pronunciavit eadem,.—Also with an inanim. object: cum Orestem fabulam doceret Euripides, primos tres versus revocasse dicitur Socrates,to have encored,. —Absol.: revocasse et repeti coëgisse,.—Impers. pass.: nominatim sum appellatus in Bruto Tullius qui libertatem civibus stabiliverat. Milies revocatum est,.—
To recall from death, bring back to life: quā servetis revocatum a morte Dareta,; cf.: Paeoniis revocatum herbis et amore Dianae,: dysentericos a morte revocari,.—
Trop.
In gen., to call back, recall, resume; to withdraw, retire; to regain, recover; to draw back, draw off or away; to withhold, restrain, etc.: facilius sicut in vitibus revocantur ea, quae sese nimium profuderunt,are checked, pruned,: et vires et corpus amisi: sed si morbum depulero, facile illa revocabo, will regain, recover, : quae (studia) remissa temporibus, longo intervallo intermissa revocavi,; cf.: quod, utcunque praetermissum, revocari non posset,: praetermissa,: quae (philosophia) nunc prope dimissa revocatur,: veteres artes,: priscos mores,: antiquam duramque militiam,: quaedam exoleta,: omissa,; et saep.: nonnumquam animum incitatum revoco ipse et reflecto,; cf. : vinolenti dubitant, haesitant, revocant se interdum,recover themselves, bethink themselves,: ut quaedam contra naturam depravata restituerentur et corrigerentur ab naturā, cum se ipsa revocasset aut arte atque medicinā,had recovered herself,: revocare se non poterat familiaritate implicatus,could not withdraw,: primae revocabo exordia pugnae,; cf. : revocari in memoriam somnii,; .— Poet., with inf.: nec tamen illa suae revocatur parcere famae, nor can she be induced, persuaded, etc., : memoriam ad referendam gratiam admonitione revocare,to bring, induce,: scalam nobis in memoriam revocare, , 16, 38, 2; : in memoriam rursus revocatus,: revocat tua forma parentem (with recordor),: magni est ingenii revocare mentem a sensibus,; cf.: eos ab illā consuetudine,: quos (homines) spes praedandi studiumque bellandi ab agriculturā et cottidiano labore revocabat,: aliquam a cupiditate,: aliquem a turpissimo consilio,: aliquem a tanto scelere,; cf. : animum ab irā,: jam lapsos ab errore,: perterritos animos a metu, et saep.: ab errore ad rectiorem viam,: cum ex saevis et perditis rebus ad meliorem statum fortuna revocatur, Cic. ap. : disceptationem ab rege ad Romanos revocabant,: rebus institutis ad humanitatem atque mansuetudinem revocavit animos hominum studiis bellandi jam immanes ac feros,: ad quam eos quasi formulam dicendi revocent,: ad quae me exempla revocas,; : rem paene ad manus,: me ad pristina studia revocavi,: me ad meum munus pensumque revocabo,: se ad industriam,: se rursus ad moestitiam,: se ad se,: vilicum ad rationem,compel to an account,: libertinos ingratos revocavit in servitutem,: fortunae possessionesque omnium in dubium incertumque revocabuntur,: ad spem consulatūs in partem revocandam aspirare non auderet,to bring over to his side,: quod temporis hortorum aut villarum curae seponitur, in animum revocabo,will transfer to my mind,: abi, Quo blandae juvenum te revocant preces (= a me ad se vocant, Orell.),.—
In partic.
Pregn.: ad aliquid, to apply, reduce, refer a thing to something as a standard (syn. referre) (Ciceron.): impuri cujusdam et ambitiosi et omnia ad suam potentiam revocantis esse sententiam,: misericordiā movetur, si is, qui audit, adduci potest, ut illa, quae de altero deplorentur, ad suas res revocet,: omnia ad artem et ad praecepta,: omnia ad scientiam,: illa de urbis situ ad rationem,: rationem ad veritatem,: rem ad illam rationem conjecturamque,.—
To recall, revoke, retract, cancel (not so till after the Aug. per.): si facta mihi revocare liceret. : promissum suum,: sententiam suam,: libertatem (shortly after: in servitutem retrahi),: litteras,: legatum ad quingenta,.—
As law t. t.: domum, domum suam revocare, to appeal to a judge of one's own country or city: (legatis) revocandi domum suam jus datur, , §§ 3, 4, and 5.—
To ask back again, to invite in return: mutuo vocare, Non. (rare): domum suam istum non fere quisquam vocabat. Nec mirum; qui neque in urbe viveret neque revocaturus esset,; Varr. ap. : cum vulpem revocasset,; .—Hence, transf.: tribuni plebis quoniam adhuc praesens certamen contentionemque fugerunt: nunc in meam contionem prodeant, et, quo provocati ad me venire noluerunt, revocati saltem revertantur,i. e. now that they are invited to come back,.—
To call again, summon anew (rare): itaque hominem populus revocat, et retrahatur necesse est,i. e. to answer a renewed accusation, (6), 6: tribuni de integro agere coeperunt revocaturosque se easdem tribus renuntiarunt,; cf. : refectum est convivium et rursus Quartilla ad bibendum revocavit,challenged us again,: convivam in diem posterum,.

la:verb:revolo.html:
rĕ-vŏlo, āre, v. n.,
to fly back (rare but class.).
Lit.: turdi quotannis in Italiam trans mare advolant et eodem revolant,: grus,: mergi,: Daedalus ceratis alis,: apis ut nulla intro revolet,.—
Transf.: telum,: sol,to hasten back,: ad aliquem,.

la:verb:reverbero.html:
rĕ-verbĕro, āre, 1, v. a.,
to strike back, repel, cause to rebound (post-Aug.): sic veneficiis corpus induruit, ut saxa reverberet,: Indus saxis saepe impeditus quīs crebro reverberatur,: reverberato lapide,: ut humus molliter cedat nec incrementa duritiā suā reverberet,: usque adeo ut radios omnis nostri tuoris splendore reverberent,: hinc vi reverberante ventorum,. —
Trop.: iram Fortunae,; . 27; cf. .

la:verb:revalesco.html:
rĕ-vălesco, lŭi, 3,
v. inch. n., to grow well again; to regain one's former strength, state, or condition; to recover (poet. and post-Aug. for convalesco, reficior).
Lit., : ex capitali morbo,: interibi revalesco,: te significasti jam revalescere coepisse,. —
Trop.: Laodicea (tremore terrae prolapsa), revaluit,: diplomata Othonis, quae neglegebantur, revalescerent, regain their force or authority, : astutia,.

la:verb:revenio.html:
rĕ-vĕnĭo, vēni, ventum, 4, v. n.,
to come again, come back, to return (class.; cf.: redeo, revertor).
Lit., absol.: reveni, ut illum persequar,; so ; : domum,; ; ; ; sq.; ; cf.: domum de hippodromo,: in urbem,: huc,; ; ; : ex longinquo,—
Trop. (Plaut.): in eum nunc haec revenit res locum, ut, etc.,: cum eo reveni ex inimicitiā in gratiam,.—Impers. pass.: inter eos rursum si reventum in gratiam est, (a little before, redeunt rursum in gratiam).

la:noun:revocatio.html:
rĕvŏcātĭo, ōnis, f.
id.
,
a calling back or away, a recalling (rare but good prose).
Lit.: a bello (with receptui signum),.—
Transf., in plur.: revocationes lunae a sole,—
Trop.: revocatio ad contemplandas voluptates,. —
Ejusdem verbi crebrius positi quaedam distinctio et revocatio, i.e. qualification and withdrawal, as a fig. of speech, ; .—
As law t. t., the right of one absent from home to appeal to a court of his own state or country, (cf. revoco, B. 2. c.).

la:verb:reviresco.gloss: to become green or verdant again
senses: to become green or verdant again
la:verb:reviresco.html:
rĕ-vĭresco, rŭi, 3,
v. inch. n., to become or grow green again; to recover its verdure.
Lit. (rare): laesae silvae,: arbor Ruminalis in novos fetus,: caepe revirescit decedente lunā, contra autem inarescit adulescente,.—
Poet., transf., of an old man, to become young again: spes est virginibus subjecta, Arte suum parili revirescere posse parentem,: pars credunt torvos patriā revirescere vultus,.—
Trop., to grow strong or vigorous again; to grow young again; to be renewed; to flourish again; to revive (freq. and class.): aliquando rei publicae vires, quae malitiā nocentum exaruerunt, virtute optimatium revirescent,; cf.: quamquam sunt accisae (res), tamen efferent se aliquando et ad renovandum bellum revirescent,; : cum semel invasit senectus, regressum non habet, nec revirescere aut repubescere potest, ; Flor. prooem. fin.: imperium,: domus Germanici,: partes,: dux pignore promissae laudis,: nunc praeclari facti decus crebrā memoriā revirescit,.

la:verb:revinco.html:
rĕ-vinco, vīci, victum, 3, v. a.,
to conquer, subdue.
Lit. (only poet., and in Tac.): victrices catervae Consiliis juvenis revictae,; cf.: revicta conjuratio,repressed, checked,: primordia rerum aliquā ratione,: vires (ignis),.—
Trop., to convict; to refute, disprove (class.; syn.: convinco, refuto),: numquam hic neque suo neque amicorum judicio revincetur, * : aliquem,: aliquem in mendacio,: aliquem in culpā et in maleficio,: crimina rebus revicta,disproved, (with confutare verbis); : crimen,: testimoniis revinci,
